china.figure: No charge found in the rules read
china.explain: None of the rules read for this guide charges a tax on the conversion or the remittance itself. What the bank checks is that tax on the underlying income was already paid. This is a reading of the cited rules, not a certified statement.
Progressive rates. Normally withheld by the employer; the tax record is the voucher the bank asks for. If already taxed, the rules read add nothing more when you convert.
Gain = sale income less original value and reasonable expenses. The tax voucher is required to remit the proceeds.
Charged on each payment. Treaty relief and the treatment of bank-deposit interest were not verified.
Progressive rates for individual business income.
The tax above for that type of income becomes due first; without the voucher the bank cannot convert. Late-payment surcharge and fines were seen only in an excerpt and are left blank.

china.item: Tax-filing form for a single payment above USD 50,000
china.explain: A filing, not a tax. Required for listed items such as work pay, dividends and property-sale income paid abroad.

china_penalties.item: Evading FX controls (moving funds abroad in breach of the rules)
china_penalties.figure: Up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% if serious
china_penalties.explain: Plus criminal liability where a crime is constituted.

china_penalties.item: Buying foreign exchange with false or invalid documents
china_penalties.figure: Up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% if serious

china_penalties.item: Private or disguised trading of foreign exchange
china_penalties.figure: Up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% if serious
china_penalties.explain: Illegal gains confiscated; criminal liability where a crime is constituted.

china_penalties.item: Carrying foreign currency across the border in breach of the rules

china_penalties.explain: Prohibited by the Individual FX Measures; the fine scale that applies depends on how the breach is classified, so no figure is stated.

us.item: Wiring your own money into the US
us.figure: No charge found in the pages read
us.explain: A US citizen is taxed on worldwide income when it is earned, wherever it sits. The pages read state no tax on moving money you already own; this is a reading, not a certified statement.

us.item: Income earned in China (salary, interest, gains)
us.explain: Reportable in the year earned, translated to USD at the rate when received. If it was not reported in earlier years, that is the US exposure — not the transfer.
Claim on Form 1116. Not available for income excluded under the foreign earned income exclusion.

us.item: Exchange gain when the CNY is converted
us.explain: For a personal transaction, a gain from rate changes is ignored unless it exceeds USD 200. Treatment above USD 200 and of losses was not verified.

us.figure: Does not apply to money arriving
us.explain: Applies to remittances sent from the United States to recipients abroad when funded with cash or a similar physical instrument.

us_reporting.figure: Over USD 10,000 at any time in the year
us_reporting.explain: Aggregate of all foreign accounts. Due April 15, automatic extension to October 15. Filed online, not with the tax return.
Maximum amounts for penalties assessed on or after 2025-01-17.

us_reporting.figure: Over USD 50,000 at year end or USD 75,000 at any time
us_reporting.explain: Unmarried, living in the US. Married filing jointly: USD 100,000 / 150,000. Living abroad: USD 200,000 / 300,000 (jointly USD 400,000 / 600,000).
USD 10,000 for failure to disclose plus USD 10,000 per 30 days after IRS notice.
From a nonresident alien or foreign estate. Relevant to inheritance and to money routed through other people.
Report when entering or leaving the US; the threshold applies to a family or group together. Unreported cash can be seized.
